title: Best Entryway Benches 2026: 5 Picks for Small Spaces
description: Best entryway benches of 2026 — West Elm, CB2, IKEA, Pottery Barn, and Wayfair compared on upholstery durability, storage, and entry space proportions.
lede: An entryway bench solves a specific problem: somewhere to sit while putting on shoes without holding onto the wall, and somewhere to set down bags before sorting through them. The right bench fits the space without blocking the door swing, has a seat height that's actually useful for shoe-changing, and either looks good enough to leave visible or has storage underneath to justify its footprint. These five cover every realistic budget and use case.
methodology: Each bench was evaluated on seat height for functional shoe-changing (16-18 inches is the target), stability under 200+ lb loads, upholstery durability for entryway conditions, and whether storage features justify the space cost. We did not test these products ourselves.

sections.heading: What to Look for in an Entryway Bench
paragraphs: Most benches that fail in entryways do so because they weren't sized right for the space or because the upholstery couldn't handle entryway conditions. Both are preventable.

subsections.heading: Seat Height for Shoe-Changing
paragraphs: For functional shoe-changing, a seat height of 16-18 inches works for most adults. Shorter than 16 inches makes getting up awkward; taller than 20 inches means your feet don't reach the floor comfortably. Standard dining chair height is 17-19 inches, which is a good reference. If the bench will primarily be used by children, a lower seat height (12-14 inches) makes more sense.

subsections.heading: Upholstery Durability in an Entryway Context
paragraphs: Entryways are hard on fabric: people sit in wet coats, bags drag across the seat, and the space sees more varied traffic than any other room. Performance fabrics (olefin, crypton, microfiber) handle moisture and abrasion better than linen or velvet. Leather and faux leather wipe clean but can crack in cold entry areas. If the bench will sit near an exterior door, avoid any fabric that deteriorates with repeated moisture exposure.

subsections.heading: Storage vs. Open Base
paragraphs: Under-bench storage (drawers, lift-top compartments, or open cubbies) can hold shoes, gloves, and small bags. This is useful if the entryway doesn't have a separate shoe cabinet. Open-leg benches are visually lighter and easier to clean underneath. A bench with shoe cubbies built in is the most efficient single piece for a small entry, but it's also heavier and less versatile if the room changes.

subsections.heading: Size and Door Clearance
paragraphs: Measure from the interior wall to where the door stops when fully open — that's the maximum bench depth. Most entryway benches are 16-18 inches deep, which gives comfortable door clearance in standard entries. Width should be proportional to the wall — a 48-inch bench against a 60-inch wall looks right; the same bench in a 40-inch entryway blocks the path. For very narrow entries (under 48 inches total), consider a backless, wall-hugging design.

sections.heading: How These Five Stack Up
paragraphs: West Elm's Upholstered Entry Bench is the best all-purpose choice for a furnished entryway — quality upholstery, proper seat height, and a design that integrates with other furniture rather than fighting it. CB2's Camden bench is more minimal and contemporary, with a lower profile that suits modern interiors. IKEA's TRONES is unusual — it's not a traditional bench but a wall-mounted shoe-storage system with a small seated surface, which makes it ideal for very small entries.

Pottery Barn's Parkmore is the storage-forward option: lift-top compartment, hooks, and a traditional design that suits family entryways with lots of gear. Wayfair's Andover Mills is the budget value — it looks more expensive than it is, and the construction holds up for normal household use.

sections.heading: Bottom Line
paragraphs: West Elm for a furnished entryway where the bench needs to integrate visually with the rest of the room. IKEA TRONES for a very small entry where floor space is critical. Pottery Barn Parkmore for a family entry that needs genuine storage capacity. CB2 for a minimal-design home. Wayfair Andover Mills when budget is the constraint but you still want something that looks considered.

faqs.q: What height should an entryway bench be?
faqs.a: For functional shoe-changing, 16-18 inches seat height is the target for average-height adults. This is similar to standard chair height, which ensures you can sit comfortably and stand up without awkwardness. Bench heights below 15 inches require a crouching motion to sit that becomes uncomfortable quickly. Measure your own chair seat height as a reference before ordering.

faqs.q: How wide should an entryway bench be?
faqs.a: The bench should be narrower than the entry wall it sits against, leaving 12-18 inches of clear wall on at least one side. For a 60-inch wall, a 48-inch bench is proportional. For a narrow hallway entry (under 48 inches of wall width), a 36-inch bench leaves better visual balance. The practical minimum for a functional shoe-changing bench is 36 inches — shorter than that and it's more decorative than useful.

faqs.q: Should an entryway bench have storage?
faqs.a: If your entry doesn't have a coat closet or shoe cabinet, yes — under-bench storage significantly improves entryway function. Lift-top storage hides gear that would otherwise sit out. Open cubbies work well for daily-use shoes. If you already have coat storage and the bench is primarily for sitting, a simpler open-base design works well and looks less furniture-heavy in a small space.

faqs.q: What fabric holds up best on an entryway bench?
faqs.a: Performance fabrics with a stain-resistant finish (olefin, solution-dyed acrylic, or crypton-treated textiles) handle entryway conditions the best. They resist moisture from wet coats, clean up with a damp cloth, and don't absorb odors. Velvet and linen look great but show wear quickly in high-traffic entryways. Leather is durable and wipes clean but can feel cold and stiff near exterior doors in winter months.

faqs.q: Can I use a regular bedroom bench as an entryway bench?
faqs.a: Yes, if the dimensions work — the main requirement is seat height (16-18 inches) and appropriate depth for the space. Bedroom benches designed for the foot of a bed are often 48-60 inches wide and 16-18 inches deep, which works well in an entryway. The main consideration is upholstery durability: a delicate linen bedroom bench will deteriorate faster in an entryway context than it would at the foot of a bed.

products.review: West Elm's Upholstered Entry Bench is built specifically for entryway use — the performance fabric options resist the moisture and abrasion that's typical in an entry, and the seat height of 18 inches is correct for practical shoe-changing. The tapered solid wood legs give it a mid-century profile that integrates well with most furnished entries. Available in multiple fabric colors and textures. The frame is solid and doesn't flex under normal load. It's not a storage bench — purely a seating piece — but the clean design means it doesn't make the entry feel smaller.
pros: 18-inch seat height is correct for practical shoe-changing use
Performance fabric options resist moisture and entryway wear
Tapered wood legs create a proportional, furniture-quality silhouette
cons: No storage — purely a seating piece
Performance fabric requires specific care product for stain removal

products.review: CB2's Camden bench has a lower, more horizontal profile than most entryway benches — the seat sits at 17 inches, and the wide, flat cushion gives it a contemporary rather than traditional look. The legs are solid brass-finished metal, which is a design detail that elevates it visually. The cushion fabric is a woven blend that handles moderate wear. It's not as storage-oriented as the Pottery Barn option, but for a modern or minimal home where the entryway is visible from the main living area, the Camden doesn't interrupt the design language.
pros: Brass-finished metal legs add a premium design detail
Low horizontal profile works in modern and minimal interiors
Properly sized 17-inch seat height for adult shoe-changing
cons: Woven cushion fabric shows pet hair more than performance alternatives

products.review: IKEA's TRONES is wall-mounted, which means it takes zero floor space when you're not using it. It's primarily a shoe storage cabinet — each unit holds shoes in flip-down compartments — but the closed fronts provide a sitting surface when filled. For an entry under 40 inches wide where floor space is genuinely critical, TRONES is the only functional option in this group. You can mount two or three units side by side for a 40-60 inch storage bench. Assembly is simple; wall mounting requires proper stud or anchor hardware.
pros: Wall-mounted — takes no floor space, critical in small entries
Each unit stores 3-4 pairs of shoes in flip-down compartments
Multiple units can be combined for wider storage coverage
cons: Sitting surface is the closed cabinet top — no cushioning
Must be properly wall-anchored — stud finder and correct hardware required

products.review: Pottery Barn's Parkmore bench is the most storage-forward piece in this group: a lift-top compartment holds seasonal gear, hooks on the back panel hold bags and coats, and the cushioned seat provides actual comfort. It's a one-piece entryway solution for families that need gear organization without a full mudroom. The traditional design with paneled sides and turned feet suits period homes and family houses. The lift-top hinge is smooth and holds open properly without requiring one hand to keep it up.
pros: Lift-top storage holds seasonal items and bags out of sight
Back-panel hooks add coat and bag hanging without a separate rack
Smooth lift-top hinge holds open hands-free
cons: Traditional design limits compatibility with modern or minimal rooms
Heavier than open-base alternatives — difficult to reposition alone

products.review: Wayfair's Andover Mills bench does a convincing impression of a mid-range piece at a budget price. The tufted upholstery and tapered legs create a visual quality that doesn't immediately telegraph the low price. The construction is lighter than West Elm or Pottery Barn, but the frame is stable under normal adult weight and the fabric doesn't deteriorate in the first year. For a guest room entry, a rental apartment, or anywhere you want a functional bench without committing to a permanent furniture investment, this is the most honest budget choice.
pros: Tufted upholstery looks more expensive than the price suggests
Stable frame handles normal adult weight without flexing
Available in multiple fabric colors to match existing furniture
cons: Lighter construction — not suitable for heavy daily commercial-style use
Fabric is basic polyester blend, not a performance fabric

pinDescription: Five entryway benches compared for small spaces and heavy use — from IKEA's wall-mounted TRONES to Pottery Barn's lift-top storage bench. Find the right fit for your entry.
